To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the oil palm boom is associated with the production of a highly mobile, geographically diffuse and socially heterogeneous land ownership structure in Indonesia; 2) the oil palm wealth generated by this land ownership structure has contributed to patterns of labour mobility that are associated with the reproduction of social inequality; and 3) this process of social differentiation is not limited to the oil palm plantations, but also affects the rural communities that are located in the hinterland of the oil palm plantation belt.

oil palm wealth has been a major contributor to land accumulation in Indonesia and that the resulting patterns of land ownership and labour mobility are geographically diffuse and contribute to social differentiation.
the oil palm boom has contributed to the creation of new forms of land accumulation and labour mobility in Indonesia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.

the ways in which the oil palm agribiz- nesseconomic model shapes the social relations of production and the social and economic consequences of these changes for rural livelihoods and social differentiation.
the ways in which the accumulation of land and capital by oil palm companies in Indonesia is linked to the production of labour and land mobility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current land and labour regimes in the oil palm industry are not sustainable.

the oil palm agribusines model in Indonesia has contributed to the reproduction of a highly unequal and exploitative social structure, and the paper concludes by arguing for a more equitable distribution of land and labour.

the oil palm boom has contributed to a process of land accumulation that is geographically diffuse, but that has also contributed to the production and reproduction of a labour force that is highly mobile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ongoing oil palm boom is contributing to the reproduction of a highly differentiated social structure throughout the country.
the oil palm boom in Kalimantan has contributed to a geographically diffuse pattern of wealth accumulation, land ownership and labour mobility in Indonesia.
the oil palm boom in Kalimantan is not only about land and labour, but also about the production of new forms of social relations and social differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oil palm boom is not a rural phenomenon but rather a national one, with far-reaching effects on the lives of people across Indonesia.

the oil palm industry has contributed to an ongoing process of labour mobility and the production of a land accumulation regime that is not confined to the plantation belt but rather is a national phenomenon.
the ongoing oil palm boom is a significant contributor to the production of land inequality in Indonesia.
